text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Thursday.
- Croatian Refugee Association director Mato Simic claims before release of official election results that the Croats have won elections in Serbn enclave towns of Vukovar and Ilok.
- European Bank for Reconstruction and Development has so far injected some 2.4 billion kuna into Croatian projects.
- Croatian government will not discuss cutting import tax on cars before the year is over.

- Croatian Party of Rights chairman Anto Dapic distances himself from events that may harm Croatia's image following an article on alleged rebirth of fascism in Croatia published by the New York Times.
- Who the new Zagreb mayor will be should be known at the end of May.
- Some 284,611 unemployed registered in Croatia in March, up 1.9 percent from February and 7.8 percent from March 1996.
- Croatia's internal debt totals 4.96 billion kuna, according to Finance Ministry.
- Repatriation project for Serb refugees who want to return to the areas liberated during "Operation Storm" is being prepared through joint efforts of Croatian government, UNTAES and UNHCR.

- Canadian authorities have issued special forms for Croatian and Bosnian citizens who want to travel there. Forms contain questions like what the person was doing during the war. Visitors from Yugoslavia do not have to fill in such form.

- We will forge a coalition with the opposition and not with the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) in its present form, says Social Democratic Party (SDP) deputy president Zdravko Tomac in an interview.
- Three more companies join Kaptol Banka Group: A commercial agency, a brokerage and a company for the leasing of equiment are established. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
